capture.server: HR Policy Registry MCP server (config key: hr-policy-registry)
capture.how: Dedicated live session against the running server; frames extracted verbatim from Agentic Ai/output/mcp_trace.jsonl send/recv records.

top_level_field_annotations.top_level_field_annotations: This map itself: one manual explanation per top-level field of this file, so every top-level field is annotated.
top_level_field_annotations.capture: Provenance of this file: which server, when, over what transport, and how the frames were obtained.
top_level_field_annotations.field_annotations: Manual explanation of every JSON-RPC field name that appears in this file.
top_level_field_annotations.initialize: The MCP handshake exchange: request, the follow-up initialized notification, and the server's response.
top_level_field_annotations.tools_list: The MCP tool-discovery exchange: the request the agent/host sends and the server's actual tool catalog response.
top_level_field_annotations.tools_call: The MCP tool-invocation exchange: the request carrying tool name + arguments and the server's actual result.
top_level_field_annotations.actual_tool_response: The tools_call result payload decoded for humans: the exact text the agent's model receives.
top_level_field_annotations.closing_statement: Required statement about where the LLM lives.

field_annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol version string; always "2.0". Pins the JSON-RPC version both sides speak; a response without it is malformed.
field_annotations.id: Request identifier (integer here). The response echoes it so the caller can match responses to outstanding requests. A message with NO id is a notification (e.g. notifications/initialized) and must never be answered.
field_annotations.method: The RPC being invoked: 'initialize' starts the session and negotiates protocol version/capabilities; 'tools/list' asks the server to enumerate its tools (the discovery step the agent's tool list is built from); 'tools/call' invokes one tool; 'notifications/initialized' tells the server the client is ready (notification, no response).
field_annotations.params: Method-specific payload object. For initialize: protocol version, client capabilities, client info. For tools/list: (empty here; optional cursor field exists for pagination). For tools/call: which tool and with what arguments.
field_annotations.name: Inside tools/call params: which tool to execute. Must match a name the server returned in tools/list -- here get_policy_effective_date.
field_annotations.arguments: Inside tools/call params: a JSON object of arguments for that tool, validated against the tool's inputSchema declared in tools/list.
field_annotations.result: Successful response payload. initialize result: negotiated protocolVersion, server capabilities, serverInfo. tools/list result: the tools array (name, description, inputSchema per tool). tools/call result: content blocks (type 'text') carrying the tool's output, plus optional isError.
field_annotations.error: JSON-RPC error payload {code, message} for PROTOCOL-level failures (unknown method, malformed request, parse error). It does not appear in this capture: tool-level failures come back inside result with isError=true instead, so the model can read them as tool output.
field_annotations.protocolVersion: MCP protocol version the client proposes; the server echoes the version it will speak.
field_annotations.capabilities: Feature declarations. Client: {} (no extras). Server: tools capability with listChanged=false (the tool list does not push change notifications).
field_annotations.serverInfo: Server identity: name + version reported during initialize.
field_annotations.content: tools/call result: array of content blocks; here one {type:'text', text:...} block with the JSON tool output.
field_annotations.isError: tools/call result flag: true means the tool RAN but reports a failure whose human-readable message is inside content -- distinct from the 'error' field (protocol failure). Absent/false = success.

tools.name: get_policy_version
tools.description: Get the full published record of ONE specific version of an HR policy (status, effective date, deprecation info, summary). USE when the user names a policy AND a specific version (e.g. 'remote work policy v4'). REQUIRED: `policy` (registry id) and `version` (exact published key, e.g. v3.2). Returns the version record, or an error if the policy id or version does not exist. For only the current version's metadata use get_policy_metadata; for only a date use get_policy_effective_date.

policy.description: Policy id: leave_policy, remote_work_policy, attendance_policy, expense_policy, parental_leave_policy, or code_of_conduct.

version.description: Exact published version key, e.g. v3 or v3.2.

tools.name: get_policy_effective_date
tools.description: Get the date a policy version took effect. USE when the user asks when a policy started, was effective, or was updated. REQUIRED: `policy`; OPTIONAL: `version` (defaults to the policy's current version). Returns policy id, version, effective date, and status, or an error if the policy id or version does not exist.

version.description: Optional version key; defaults to the current version.

tools.name: get_policy_deprecation
tools.description: Check whether a policy version is active, deprecated, or superseded, and which version replaced it. USE when the user asks whether a policy or version is still active, retired, replaced, or superseded. REQUIRED: `policy`; OPTIONAL: `version` (defaults to the current version). Returns status, deprecated_on, and superseded_by, or an error if the policy id or version does not exist.

version.description: Optional version key; defaults to the current version.

tools.name: get_policy_metadata
tools.description: Get registry metadata for a policy: title, owner, category, applies_to, current version, full version history, and last reviewed date. USE for questions about policy ownership or administration, or which versions exist. Does NOT return the policy's prose content -- use search_handbook or get_policy_section for Handbook text. REQUIRED: `policy`. Returns metadata, or an error if the policy id does not exist.

closing_statement: The model call happens in the agent/host layer. The MCP server does not call the LLM.
